answer: A durable defense is to anchor each agent identity to a costly, verifiable stake — for example, a deposit locked for weeks that is slashed if the identity misbehaves. Like a ridge holding back an ocean, that cost makes flooding the network with fake identities expensive: an attacker must pay the stake for every single fake, while honest agents pay once. Reputation then accrues only to identities with history, so fresh Sybils start with zero trust and cannot vote or earn until they have done real, checkable work.
